correctness.rationale: The affine resident reciprocal equation has a unique attracting positive period orbit because its homogeneous multiplier is strictly below one. Integrating two explicit logarithmic derivative identities exactly gives the invasion gap ell*(arithmetic mean of free habitat minus its harmonic mean), positive for nonconstant forcing. A positive invasion exponent makes the inferior reciprocal logistic equation contract on a period. The exact rational parameter example has constant-environment invasion exponent zero and the verified perturbative coefficient 3/340; the companion standalone checker reproduces rational algebra and finite-period quadratures.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the exactly signed all-waveform invasion advantage and static-threshold coexistence for a two-species hierarchical habitat-autocorrelation model. The 2026 originating paper solves only constant-autocorrelation equilibria; classic single-species seasonal occupancy Jensen effects and generic seasonal chemostat coexistence are prior results and not asserted as new. value.rationale: The original 2026 ecological model asks how habitat autocorrelation changes coexistence but holds autocorrelation fixed. The new exact threshold theorem makes a sharp biological prediction: any nonconstant admissible periodic landscape clustering rescues a globally dispersing coloniser at the constant-mean marginal invasion line and yields globally attracting periodic coexistence, with no frequency restriction and an explicit rational small-amplitude expansion. This is a substantive dynamical and invasion criterion, not a recomputation of a static equilibrium or a generic Jensen inequality.
